data.narrative:
Neros is a Series C defense and security company founded by Soren Monroe-Anderson and Olaf Hichwa, currently valued at $2.5B post-money following $250M in total capital raised. The valuation assessment draws on a peer universe of 15 same-sector and same/adjacent-stage companies, comprising 8 private firms and 2 public comparables (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS). Key private peers include Castelion ($13.0B, Series C), Stark Defence ($4.0B, Series C), Saronic ($9.2B, Series D), and Quantum-Systems ($8.0B, Series D).

Two triangulation methods prove applicable. Stage-progression methodology applies a typical 1.7x step-up multiplier to the $2.5B last post-money valuation, implying $4.2B at the next funding stage. Peer-median analysis across the 15-company comp set yields a median valuation of $2.2B, though the range spans $300M to $13.0B, reflecting meaningful dispersion within the defense tech sector at this stage.

Synthesizing these approaches produces a triangulated valuation range of $1.9B (low) to $4.9B (high), with a median of $3.2B. The current $2.5B valuation sits below the implied median, reflecting either relative undervaluation or stage-specific positioning within the distribution. Key uncertainties center on stage-progression timing, the wide peer valuation dispersion, and sector-specific risk factors not quantified here.
